questions.title: Gamma-Poisson Bayesian online changepoint detection from paper and data
questions.description: Focused L2 paper-to-code reproduction based on Adams and MacKay (2007). The model-visible source snapshot contains the exact arXiv author source, Algorithm 1, and the public boot coal-disaster event dates and documentation. Public reference implementations and all gold outcomes are withheld from runtime. Let x_1,...,x_T be nonnegative integer counts. Within each product partition, counts are iid Poisson with a segment-specific rate; independent segment rates have a Gamma(shape a, rate b) prior. Use the paper's Algorithm 1 convention: before x_t, each prior run-length hypothesis has its own posterior predictive; the same predictive term enters the growth and changepoint branches, the constant hazard h is applied after that predictive factor, and the zero-run state resets its sufficient statistics to the prior for the next datum. In one authoritative Markdown/LaTeX Theory workspace, derive the Gamma-Poisson predictive mass, the log-space growth and changepoint recursions, normalization, sufficient-statistic updates, initialization, and indexing. Prove from this declared constant-hazard convention that the normalized row-zero probability equals h at every processed time, and explain why row zero alone is therefore not a changepoint score. Explain causal prefix invariance, finite-horizon complexity, and the distinction between exact filtering under the model and evidence that the model is scientifically adequate. The required model-authored Python artifact is est_bocd_gamma_poisson and must implement run_estimator(request) under the closed contract below without author or reference code. Exploratory Python or R may check formulas. A separately frozen confirmatory assessment uses four 120-observation single-change Poisson designs with the change before observation 61, rate pairs (1,8), (8,1), (1,4), and (4,1), Gamma(1,1), h=0.01, and at least 1000 fresh replicates per design. A detection occurs when the returned MAP run length is at most 5 for some observation 61 through 71; a pre-change false reset occurs when it is at most 5 for some observation 31 through 60. For each design, report detection probability, false-reset probability, conditional detection delay, and Monte Carlo standard errors. The confirmatory target is detection probability at least 0.75 and false-reset probability at most 0.10 in every declared design, assessed with a pre-outcome one-sided two-standard-error margin. Separately bin all 191 supplied coal event dates by floor(date) for calendar years 1851 through 1962, preserving zero-count years, and run the same estimator with Gamma(1,1) and h=1/30; report exact input identity and posterior/MAP summaries without claiming that one annual rebin reproduces the paper's weekly figure or identifies a causal effect of the 1887 Act. These algorithm and empirical checks are finite-design evidence, not proof of changepoint recovery outside the declared model, author-code replication, novelty, or formal proof. Lean formalization is not applicable, and unresolved indexing, numerical, source, or scientific-scope gaps must remain explicit.

public_data.name: coal
public_data.source_reference: Jarrett (1979), A note on the intervals between coal-mining disasters, Biometrika 66, 191-193

request_fields.name: counts
request_fields.meaning: Observed Poisson counts in causal time order.
request_fields.shape: one array containing 1 through 512 exact integers
request_fields.indexing: counts[i] is x_{i+1}; no future count may affect an earlier posterior row
request_fields.edge_cases: Reject booleans, floats, strings, nulls, nested values, negative counts, counts above 10000, an empty array, or more than 512 observations. Do not coerce, round, drop, pad, or truncate values.

request_fields.name: hazard_probability
request_fields.meaning: Constant per-step changepoint hazard h used in both branches of Algorithm 1.
request_fields.shape: one finite non-Boolean scalar strictly between 0 and 1
request_fields.indexing: the same value applies at every time and prior run length
request_fields.edge_cases: Reject zero, one, out-of-range, nonfinite, Boolean, string, null, array, or object values rather than clipping or coercing them.

request_fields.name: gamma_shape
request_fields.meaning: Prior Gamma shape a for each newly reset segment rate.
request_fields.indexing: the same prior shape initializes every zero-run state
request_fields.edge_cases: Reject nonpositive, above-domain, nonfinite, Boolean, string, null, array, or object values rather than clipping or coercing them.

request_fields.name: gamma_rate
request_fields.meaning: Prior Gamma rate b, not scale, for each newly reset segment rate.
request_fields.indexing: the same prior rate initializes every zero-run state
request_fields.edge_cases: Reject nonpositive, above-domain, nonfinite, Boolean, string, null, array, or object values rather than clipping, inverting, or coercing them.

response_fields.name: run_length_posterior
response_fields.meaning: Causal posterior probability rows for run length after each processed prefix, including initialization.
response_fields.shape: exactly T+1 rows; row 0 is [1.0], and row t has exactly t+1 finite probabilities indexed r=0,...,t
response_fields.indexing: row t conditions only on counts[0:t]; row t entry r is the normalized Algorithm 1 mass for r_t=r
response_fields.edge_cases: Every value is in [0,1], each row sums to one within floating roundoff, impossible upper-triangular states are absent rather than padded, and under this constant-hazard convention row t entry 0 equals h within floating roundoff for every t>=1.
response_fields.normalization: Use log-space predictive and branch weights, normalize each complete row once, and return ordinary probabilities.

response_fields.name: map_run_length
response_fields.meaning: Maximum a posteriori run length for each noninitial posterior row.
response_fields.indexing: entry t-1 is the smallest r attaining the maximum in posterior row t
response_fields.edge_cases: Every entry lies in 0,...,t and ties choose the smallest run length without a tolerance.
response_fields.normalization: Direct argmax of the returned row.

response_fields.name: log_evidence
response_fields.meaning: Incremental log predictive evidence for each observed count under the previous normalized run-length mixture.
response_fields.indexing: entry t-1 is log P(x_t | x_1,...,x_{t-1}) under the declared recursion
response_fields.edge_cases: Do not return cumulative evidence, likelihood density, base-10 logarithms, nulls, or infinities.
response_fields.normalization: Log-sum-exp of the complete changepoint and growth branch weights before row normalization.

invariants.meaning: The request contains exactly the four declared fields and the response contains exactly the three declared fields. Missing, extra, malformed, nonfinite, or out-of-domain values are rejected rather than ignored, coerced, clipped, padded, or truncated.
Repeated calls with the same request return the same JSON value and do not mutate the request, use random state, access files, invoke subprocesses, or use the network.

For any valid sequence and any nonempty prefix, running the prefix alone returns exactly the corresponding prefix of all three outputs up to floating roundoff; future counts cannot change an earlier row, MAP value, or log evidence.

Because the same predictive mixture multiplies both branches before normalization, every noninitial posterior row has row-zero probability equal to hazard_probability within floating roundoff. This identity is an indexing and implementation check, not a useful changepoint score.

For a prior-run hypothesis with Gamma(shape,rate) before count x, the predictive is the Gamma-Poisson mass; its growth child uses Gamma(shape+x,rate+1), while the zero-run child for the next observation resets to the original prior.

empirical_claims.meaning: Before outcomes, freeze the four declared single-change Poisson designs, exact change index, rates, Gamma prior, hazard, fresh seeds, at least 1000 replicates per design, estimator invocation, detection and false-reset events, conditional delay rule, Monte Carlo standard errors, and one-sided two-standard-error joint decision rule.

In every declared design, detection probability is at least 0.75 and pre-change false-reset probability is at most 0.10 when assessed using the frozen one-sided two-standard-error margin. Conditional detection delay is descriptive and receives no undeclared success threshold.

The coal application uses all 191 supplied dates exactly once, bins by floor(date) into every calendar year 1851 through 1962 including zero-count years, and invokes the same estimator with Gamma(1,1) and h=1/30. Its posterior and MAP summaries are descriptive finite-data evidence, not a weekly figure replication or causal estimate.

The confirmatory assessment tests implementation and finite-design behavior only. It does not prove exact filtering, universal changepoint recovery, scientific adequacy of piecewise Poisson sampling, historical causality, author-code replication, novelty, or formal correctness.

estimator_execution_contract.termination_guarantee: For every valid request, run_estimator performs finite O(T^2) Gamma-Poisson predictive and branch arithmetic over at most 512 observations, stores the declared triangular posterior, and returns exactly one response without randomization, file access, network access, subprocesses, or request mutation.
